AI & Cybersecurity Insights

Your weekly briefing on the cutting edge of technology

This edition sits at the collision point of two accelerating stories: AI systems are becoming autonomous enough to run their own attacks and make their own scientific discoveries — and the legal and policy scaffolding around them is straining to keep up. From a self-directed malware C2 to a self-directed enzyme discovery, the line between 'tool' and 'agent' keeps blurring. Meanwhile, courts are being asked to referee fights over who controls AI vendors and who controls the narrative on government-run platforms. Read on for the week's sharpest signals on where AI power is actually flowing.
